ca_parking_lot_crag.blurb: A single buttress on Casa Diablo Mountain in the Eastern Sierra, around 7,400 feet and a long dirt drive out from the Mammoth side of the Long Valley Caldera. It holds 19 climbs, nearly all of them bolted sport routes plus a couple of trad lines, running from about 5.4 up to 5.12. Most of the grades sit between 5.7 and 5.10, so there is plenty for mid-grade climbers and a few steps up for stronger ones. Routes are short, single-pitch lines apart from one two-pitcher, and the rock is solid. Because climbs wrap around every side of the buttress, you can usually find sun on a cold day or shade in summer. It is the first cliff you see from the parking area.

ca_king_otto_s_castle.blurb: A big, blocky formation sitting in the middle of the Indian Cove campground in Joshua Tree National Park, near 3,200 feet. The 19 climbs are mostly trad, with a couple of bolted lines and a couple of top-ropes, and the grades stretch from about 5.4 to 5.12. The heart of the spread is 5.10 and 5.11, with a handful of easier lines below it. Most of the action is on the south and west sides, where the climbing is largely thin face work with only a few good cracks. Indian Cove is lower and more sheltered than the rest of the park, which makes this a sensible winter pick.

ca_7_lewis.blurb: Sector 7 of the Silver Lake cliffs above the June Lake Loop in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 7,400 feet. The 19 climbs here are mostly top-rope lines with six bolted sport routes, and the grades are easy to moderate, running from the lowest 5.x grades up to about 5.9. That makes it a good fit for beginners, families and anyone building mileage. The quartzite is mostly sound, though some of it has seen little traffic and can still be loose, so belayers should stay well back from the base. You reach it by a steep uphill trail that meets the rock at the Trail Slab.

ca_femme_fatale_area.blurb: One of the sectors at Lizard's Mouth, a sandstone bouldering area in the hills above Santa Barbara on the Central Coast. This sector holds 19 problems and covers a wide spread: several easy problems in the V0 to V3 range, a middle group around V5 to V8, and a few much harder lines up to the V10 and V11 range. That range makes it useful for a mixed group of boulderers who want something at every level. The area as a whole is compact rather than huge, with views out over the coast, and is a pleasant stop if you are already nearby.

ca_dorm_boulder.blurb: The largest of the boulders at the Knowledge Boulders, a small bouldering spot in the Mammoth Lakes area of the Eastern Sierra at about 7,800 feet. It sits next to the student dormitory on a community college campus and has 19 problems. The range is wide and friendly: a few very easy warm-ups, a solid cluster from V2 to V4, then harder lines through V5 and V6 and one problem at V7. Most problems around this small cluster are moderate and well liked, so it works for a short session or a mixed-ability group.
